paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between rank and errors, measured in a unitless quantity. The x-axis is labeled "Rank" with a linear scale ranging from 4 to 256, with tick labels at intervals of 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis is labeled "Errors (BoolQ)" and has a linear scale from 0.0 to 0.6 with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. A single black line is plotted with green circular markers and error bars. Starting at a value of approximately 0.23 with an error bar spanning from 0.16 to 0.30 at Rank = 4, the line decreases to approximately 0.21 with an error bar spanning 0.13 to 0.29 at Rank = 16. It then increases to approximately 0.25 with an error bar spanning 0.17 to 0.33 at Rank = 64, and finally reaches approximately 0.27 with an error bar spanning 0.19 to 0.35 at Rank = 256.
